title: Practical buyers guide: managed AI endpoints — comparison and win themes
content:
Purpose
------
Quick internal reference for AEs/SDRs/AMs and solutions engineers when selling Redwood against hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS, GCP, Azure). Focus: pragmatic buyer questions, how to steer conversations toward Redwood strengths, and short scripts + demo checklist.

Audience and buying motions
--------------------------
- Platform/Infra teams evaluating managed endpoints to avoid building an inference stack.
- Product/ML teams prioritizing time-to-market + predictable latency.
- Security/compliance buyers who need private deployment or strict data controls.
- Economic buyers (fin/ops) focused on unit cost, committed vs. variable spend.

Top decision criteria we see in RFPs and discovery (translated to buyer language)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Latency predictability and p95 SLOs
   - "Can you guarantee consistent tail latency for user-facing features?"
   - Hyperscalers: often high variance at scale (multitenant throttling, noisy neighbors), exposed cold-start behavior.
   - Redwood angle: dedicated capacity, warm allocation semantics, routing policy for low-latency fallbacks.

2) Unit economics and cost transparency
   - "What will this cost me at 10M tokens/month?"
   - Hyperscalers: opaque per-invocation and infra charge stacking; discounts buried in enterprise negotiations.
   - Redwood angle: profile-based recommendations, batching/caching controls, clear per-token and per-embedding line items; Optimize suggestions to reduce cost without quality regressions.

3) Control & observability
   - "How do we debug hallucinations, regressions, or cost spikes?"
   - Hyperscalers: basic metrics + logs; full tracing/route-level cost breakdown limited.
   - Redwood angle: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, request traces, rollout-tracking tied to prompt sets and evals.

4) Data residency / security / compliance
   - "Can this run in our VPC or on-prem? What about KMS/HSM?"
   - Hyperscalers: solutions exist, but often require custom engineering or heavyweight contracts.
   - Redwood angle: Private deployments (VPC + on-prem package) with streamlined onboarding, KMS integrations, audit logs as part of product.

5) Operational burden and vendor lock
   - "If we grow, will we be stuck on a single cloud vendor for performance reasons?"
   - Hyperscalers: tight ecosystem tie; migrations costly.
   - Redwood angle: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private; customers can move between modes without API changes.

Competitor summary (short hatchets and praise)
---------------------------------------------
- AWS (SageMaker Endpoints / Bedrock):
  - Strengths: enterprise contracts, broad ML integrations, single-vendor cloud story for infra teams.
  - Weaknesses: cost stacking, conservative performance defaults, limited model-level observability for inference products.
  - Typical buyer concerns to probe: multi-account routing, cross-region fallbacks, tail latency at scale.

- GCP (Vertex AI + Matching Engine):
  - Strengths: strong ML tooling, good data platform integration for customers on GCP.
  - Weaknesses: pricing and operational assumptions oriented toward training-first workflows; inference-specific optimizations sometimes behind APIs.
  - Typical probe: how do they handle KV cache warmups and bursty chat workloads?

- Azure (Azure OpenAI / Managed Endpoints):
  - Strengths: enterprise security and identity, Microsoft ecosystem.
  - Weaknesses: model availability lag, fewer inference-specific runtime innovations exposed to customers.
  - Typical probe: support for hybrid on-prem plus cloud in regulated industries.

Win themes and short scripts (pick-and-use)
-------------------------------------------
Use these as short soundbites in discovery / demos. Keep them concrete and tied to buyer outcomes.

1) "Predictable latency, not best-effort"
   - Script: "Many teams start with cloud endpoints and hit unpredictable p95s during peak traffic. Redwood dedicates capacity and routes intelligently so your SLAs stay intact even when usage spikes."

2) "Show me the dollars, not the surprise bills"
   - Script: "We'll model your workload with your actual prompts and show per-route token costs, then propose batching/caching knobs that reduce spend by a measurable percent — before you commit."

3) "One API across hosted, dedicated, and private"
   - Script: "You can prototype on our hosted API and then slip into dedicated or private deployment without changing code — fewer migration headaches, consistent observability."

4) "Operational escape hatches"
   - Script: "We support automatic fallback policies to smaller models or another region if capacity is constrained — your product stays online rather than erroring out under load."

Rebuttals to common hyperscaler pushbacks
-----------------------------------------
- "We already use X cloud for everything; adding another vendor is overhead."
  - Rebuttal: "We integrate with your cloud identity and VPCs; customers keep a single cloud bill and use Redwood for the inference layer where it adds most value."

- "Hyperscalers give us deep discounts at scale."
  - Rebuttal: "For many workloads, smarter batching, caching, and quantization saves more than commodity discounts — and those techniques are productized in Redwood Optimize so your ops team doesn't have to invent them."

- "We need guaranteed uptime and SLAs; cloud providers have enterprise SLAs."
  - Rebuttal: "Redwood Dedicated comes with SLA-backed capacity and predictable throughput; we also provide automated fallbacks so user-facing features degrade gracefully rather than failing hard."

Buyer / Demo checklist (for SEs)
-------------------------------
- Pre-call: get sample prompts, expected RPS, and critical latency SLOs.
- Live demo steps:
  1) Run a baseline generate on hosted mode and show token-level latency/cost.
  2) Toggle batching/caching settings (simulate burst) and show immediate cost/latency shift.
  3) Show rollout UI: a canary swap and tracing through a failing prompt set.
  4) If buyer cares about privacy: walk through private deployment onboarding doc and how KMS is integrated.
- Post-demo deliverable: a 1-pager cost/latency model using buyer prompts (attach as follow-up).

Tactical asks for GTM and product
--------------------------------
- Engineering: export a short "demo dataset" script that converts a customer's prompts into per-route token histograms and a cost model (JIRA: GTM-2143).
- Marketing: create one-pager templates for the three buyer personas (platform, product, security).
- Solutions: prepare two canonical demos — chat app (low-latency p95 focus) and batch-embeddings (unit-cost focus).

Open questions / follow-ups
-------------------------
- We need updated hyperscaler pricing examples (February 2026) to keep cost comparisons current — ask finance for 1-pagers.
- Validate recent internal perf benchmarks vs Vertex and SageMaker for 8k context models (SRE/bench team).

Notes to self (informal)
----------------------
- Keep rebuttals short; ops folks want numbers (p95 delta, $/1000 tokens).
- Avoid vendor bashing; emphasize tradeoffs and where Redwood uniquely reduces operational risk.
- This doc should feed into personalized playbooks for top 10 logo targets — map to industry-specific concerns (regulated fintech vs consumer chat).
